# ranwhat

> ranwhat is an open-source command-line tool for AI agent security on a developer's own machine. It reads the history Claude Code and twenty-nine other coding agents write to disk as an audit trail and reports what each agent actually did: credential reads, destructive commands, package publishing and other risky actions. It scans that history for leaked credentials (secret scanning for agent transcripts), scores what an agent's credentials allow, and flags the grants never used where the provider keeps a record. MIT licence, Python 3.9 or newer, no dependencies.

Run it without installing: `uvx ranwhat check`. Or install it: `pipx install ranwhat` or `pip install ranwhat`. No account is needed; an optional one at account.ranwhat.com manages Plus.

What goes online: `live`, `callers`, `--pull-usage` and clean's `revoke` ask only the provider that issued each token, and `update`, `login`, `whoami`, `logout` and `push` talk only to ranwhat.com. `update` fetches the capability catalogue, sending your token and nothing else. `push` sends derived metadata only, and only when you run it. Everything else reads locally and sends nothing. There is no telemetry.

Where it fits: ranwhat is the after-the-fact side of AI agent security and developer OPSEC. It shows what already ran, what leaked to disk, and what the tokens still allow. It does not block actions while an agent works unless you install its opt-in Claude Code hook (`ranwhat hook install`), and it does not detect prompt injection. `reach` reads the MCP server configuration agents keep on disk and flags risky shapes in it, but it does not inspect a server's code, its tool descriptions or skills for malicious content.

Commands:

- `ranwhat check`: watch and clean in one read-only pass. It never changes anything.
- `ranwhat watch`: sixteen rules over what the agent ran: credential access, secret-shaped strings in tool calls, package publishing, cloud resource changes, financial API calls, log or history tampering, destructive git, recursive deletion, local files uploaded with curl, scripts downloaded and run unread, files made writable by every user, container volumes wiped, encoded commands decoded and run, an instance's credentials asked of a cloud metadata service, jobs set to run at login, boot or on a schedule, and an agent's guardrails loosened (a permission, a hook, an approval or sandbox setting, or the ranwhat hook itself). `--json` prints one record per flagged call.
- `ranwhat ignore`: stops listing actions you expected. Each action watch and check list has a 16-character id; `ranwhat ignore ID` leaves that one out, or on a terminal every action like it (the same command, run in the same folder, until a date a year away), and `ranwhat ignore all` leaves out every action listed now, so later runs list only what is new. They write `~/.ranwhat/ignore` (`$RANWHAT_HOME/ignore`), a plain-text file of ids and entries (`RULE 'COMMAND' in=DIR until=YYYY-MM-DD`, matched word for word against the whole command); `--ignore PATH` uses another, such as a repository's `.ranwhatignore`. Every report says how many actions the file left out and by which line, `--no-ignore` lists them all again, and `--fail-on` counts only what is listed. A secret is never left out, a critical action only by its id or a narrow entry with `in=` and an `until=` no more than 400 days ahead, and a change an agent makes to ranwhat's own settings only once acknowledged on a terminal. `ranwhat ignore` alone lists the file and exits 3 on a line it cannot read; `ranwhat ignore -` reads the ids from `watch --json` on stdin. The hook never reads the file.
- `ranwhat clean`: finds credentials in every agent's transcripts, passwords typed into commands (`mysql -pPASSWORD`, `curl -u user:password`) among them, says what to rotate, and masks them only when asked (`--apply`, or `mask` in the review session). Backups go to `~/.ranwhat/backups`.
- `ranwhat sources`: every coding agent ranwhat reads, where it looked for each one's history, and whether it found any. `check`, `watch` and `clean` read them all by default; `--source ID` reads one, and `--path ID=PATH` reads one from elsewhere.
- `ranwhat reach`: the MCP servers agents are configured with (Claude Code's `~/.claude.json` and `.mcp.json`, and the configs of Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Windsurf and Codex), what each launches or connects to, and risky shapes: a secret inline in `env`, args, headers or the URL (masked the way `clean` masks it), a package fetched by `npx` or `uvx` with no exact version, a remote URL. Then the credential files (`.env`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.ssh/id_*` and others) an agent could read from its working directories that no Claude Code `Read(...)` deny rule covers, paths only, and a `permissions.deny` block to paste into `~/.claude/settings.json`. It writes nothing. `ranwhat reach DIR` looks at one project.
- `ranwhat scan profile.json`: scores authority, observability and reversibility for the credentials an agent holds. `--html report.html` writes a report. `--pull-usage` checks which grants were used, against the provider's own audit trail.
- `ranwhat callers`: who used a key, from the provider's own log: AWS CloudTrail by access key ID, and a GitHub organisation's audit log by token hash. `--mine CIDR` marks your own addresses, and callers outside them are flagged. Read-only.
- `ranwhat live`: the same as scan, from read-only token introspection. Pass tokens in the environment (`RANWHAT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `RANWHAT_GOOGLE_TOKEN`, `RANWHAT_SLACK_TOKEN`, `RANWHAT_STRIPE_TOKEN`), not as flags.
- `ranwhat demo`: an authority scan on a bundled example, with no setup.
- `ranwhat bench`: runs ranwhat's own detection over a made-up agent home in a temporary directory and scores it against an answer key: planted secrets that must be found, decoys that must not be reported, risky commands that must be rated, ordinary commands that must not. It lists what ranwhat is known not to catch apart from the score. Offline and read-only; `--seed N` repeats a run, and the exit status is 3 when an expectation is not met.
- `ranwhat revoke`: lists the Claude Code settings that let an agent act without asking (bypassPermissions, enableAllProjectMcpServers, allow rules for any shell command, curl, rm, git push or credential files). `--apply` takes them back and keeps a copy of each file. A leaked GitHub, Slack or Google token is revoked from clean's review with `revoke N`.
- `ranwhat hook install`: the one opt-in exception to after the fact. It adds a PreToolUse hook to Claude Code's settings (`--scope user`, `project` or `local`), and each tool call watch's rules rate high or critical then waits for the user's yes (`--mode ask`, the default) or, when critical, is refused (`--mode deny`). It judges locally and sends nothing; a call no rule rates high or critical gets no answer, and if the hook fails the call goes ahead. `ranwhat hook status` shows where it is installed and `ranwhat hook uninstall` removes it. It needs a lasting install (`uv tool install`, `pipx install` or `pip install`), not `uvx`.
- `ranwhat update`: refreshes the capability catalogue. Needs Plus, which is live: €12 a month per organisation. On a terminal, `scan`, `live` and `update --status` may add one dim line about the feed on stderr, never with `--json`; `RANWHAT_NO_HINTS=1` turns it off.
- `ranwhat login`: links this machine to an account at account.ranwhat.com. It prints a code to type at ranwhat.com/device, signed in, and saves the machine's own token at `~/.ranwhat/token` (mode 0600) for `update`. It sends no hostname, operating system or machine identifier.
- `ranwhat whoami`: the account, organisation, role and plan the saved token (or `RANWHAT_TOKEN`) belongs to.
- `ranwhat logout`: revokes this machine's token on the server and deletes it here, along with what it pushed. A subscription's or a CI token is only deleted here.
- `ranwhat push`: sends this machine's findings to your organisation's account, as derived metadata only: for each flagged action the rule ids, severities, a 16-character action id, the agent and the UTC time, plus counts and ranwhat's version. Never a command, path, evidence, working directory, session id, file content, secret, hostname or user name. Plus feature, live: `--dry-run` prints the exact JSON and sends nothing; otherwise it says what it will send and asks, and goes only to feed.ranwhat.com over HTTPS with this machine's token. Ignored actions are counted, not listed. Plus keeps each machine's latest push and a summary of earlier ones for 30 days; this is not the 13-month record, which is still coming. Findings of every linked machine are read side by side at account.ranwhat.com/findings.

Exit status for `check`, `watch` and `clean`: 0 ran, 1 an error, 2 no agent history to read. `--fail-on SEVERITY` (`medium`, `high` or `critical`) exits 3 when anything at or above it is found; every secret `clean` finds is `critical`. `--sarif PATH` writes the findings as SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning, each secret masked as the report shows it. In GitHub Actions, `uses: MatijaMiki/ranwhat@main` (the composite `action.yml` at the repository root) runs `check` with `--fail-on` and uploads the SARIF to code scanning; its `ignore-file` input names a committed ignore file, read as it was at the pull request's base or before the push. `keep N` in `clean`'s review is remembered as a keyed hash in `~/.ranwhat/known/kept.json`, so a kept value is not reported again.

Agents read: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Roo Code, Kilo Code, OpenCode, Continue, Aider, Goose, Zed, Warp, Amazon Q, Qwen Code, CodeBuddy, Grok Build, Droid, Kimi Code, Kimi CLI, Pi, Oh My Pi, Muse Code, Mistral Vibe, DeepSeek Harness and OpenClaw. `check`, `watch` and `clean` read all thirty, each from where it keeps its history, for the last 30 days by default (`--days N`). For Claude Code that is `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` and each session's `subagents/` transcripts, or the same under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects` when that is set; `--root PATH` reads another directory. Databases and compressed files are only read: the histories of Cursor, Zed, Warp, Amazon Q and OpenClaw are databases, or for Amazon Q in an IDE a file its language server rewrites every second, so `clean` finds their secrets but cannot mask them there. Windsurf keeps Cascade's own history encrypted, so ranwhat reads the plaintext transcripts its `post_cascade_response_with_transcript` hook writes to `~/.windsurf/transcripts`. Meta Muse, Grok Bot and the current Amp keep their history in their vendor's cloud, so there is nothing local to read.

`check` and `watch` hide every secret `clean` finds, anywhere in the history whatever `--days` says, in what they print. They keep an index for that in `~/.ranwhat/known/` (`$RANWHAT_HOME/known/` when set): salted fingerprints, never a secret, readable by you alone.

Not read yet: large tool outputs Claude Code stores in `<session>/tool-results/`, `~/.claude/history.jsonl`, and the events OpenClaw stores compressed and its cold transcript archives. Compressed Codex sessions (`.jsonl.zst`) are read on Python 3.14, or with the `zstd` command on the PATH.

## Docs

- [Commands](https://ranwhat.com/commands.md): every command and every flag, what each reads and what it sends
- [watch](https://ranwhat.com/watch.md): the sixteen rules, their severities, the false positives it suppresses, and where it reads from
- [clean](https://ranwhat.com/clean.md): how secrets are found, why masking is not remediation, and the review session
- [scan](https://ranwhat.com/scan.md): the three scores, evidence states, and the providers the catalogue covers
- [Install](https://ranwhat.com/install.md): uvx, pipx, pip or Homebrew, and what it reads and writes
- [FAQ](https://ranwhat.com/faq.md): what it reads, what it sends, what masking does, and where it fits in AI agent security, secret scanning and OPSEC
- [Reference](https://github.com/MatijaMiki/ranwhat/blob/main/docs/reference.md): full command reference in Markdown

## Guides

- [Guides](https://ranwhat.com/guides.md): every guide, with a one-line summary
- [AI coding agent security](https://ranwhat.com/guides/ai-coding-agent-security.md): a checklist for AI agent security on your own machine: what a coding agent can reach, the boundary around it, what it writes to disk, auditing what it ran, and scoping its tokens
- [Claude Code history](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-history.md): where transcripts live, retention, and how to purge them, plus where Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI and Qwen Code keep theirs
- [Stop Claude Code reading .env](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-env-secrets.md): Read deny rules, what they miss, the sandbox, and what to do once a secret was read
- [Claude Code audit log](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-audit-log.md): reading back what ran from the transcripts, then a hook or OpenTelemetry for a record from now on
- [Claude Code deleted my files](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-deleted-files.md): finding what was deleted and when, what rewind cannot restore, recovering from git or backups, and blocking a repeat
- [AI agent token scopes](https://ranwhat.com/guides/ai-agent-token-scopes.md): least privilege for an agent's tokens: checking what GitHub, Google, Slack, Stripe and AWS credentials allow and have used, then cutting them
- [Developer OPSEC](https://ranwhat.com/guides/developer-opsec.md): operations security for developers who use AI coding agents: where credentials sit on a laptop, what agent transcripts add, finding and rotating what is already there, and keeping secrets out of plaintext
- [Claude Code hooks for security](https://ranwhat.com/guides/claude-code-hooks-security.md): PreToolUse hooks and deny rules that block rm -rf, force pushes and .env reads, exit 2 versus JSON output, precedence, and what hooks cannot stop
- [MCP server security](https://ranwhat.com/guides/mcp-server-security-coding-agents.md): what an MCP server reaches, the documented risks, reading and scoping the config in Claude Code, and checking with ranwhat reach
- [Where AI coding agents keep history](https://ranwhat.com/guides/ai-coding-agent-history-locations.md): paths, formats and documented retention for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Aider, Windsurf, Cline and Continue, and how to clear them
- [Prompt injection in coding agents](https://ranwhat.com/guides/prompt-injection-coding-agents.md): how text in a README, issue or tool result becomes a command, the documented attack chains, and what limits the damage
- [Rotate a leaked API key](https://ranwhat.com/guides/rotate-leaked-api-key-ai-agent.md): rotate at the provider first for GitHub, AWS, Google Cloud, Slack, Stripe and the model providers, check logs, then mask transcripts and handle git history
- [Checking AI-written code](https://ranwhat.com/guides/check-ai-agent-code-is-secure.md): why an agent cannot verify its own code, the deterministic checks that can, where to run them so they cannot be skipped, and what to look for in the diff
- [Secure-by-default agent setup](https://ranwhat.com/guides/secure-by-default-ai-coding-agent-setup.md): what secure by default means for a coding agent: a combined Claude Code settings file, scoped credentials, reviewed MCP servers and hooks, and keeping a record
- [Best AI coding agent security tools](https://ranwhat.com/guides/best-ai-coding-agent-security-tools.md): six tools compared on five checks anyone can verify (agents read, blocking, stays local, open source, finds secrets in transcripts): ranwhat, Stroq, GitGuardian ggshield, Gitleaks, Snyk Agent Scan and TruffleHog, written by ranwhat's maker with the method and each tool's limits

## Project

- [Pricing](https://ranwhat.com/pricing.md): free on your own machine; Plus is €12 a month or €120 a year per organisation, bought from an account at account.ranwhat.com. Its catalogue feed, CI tokens and members are live, with the rest of Plus being built; the account itself, and a token per machine from `ranwhat login`, are free. Team is annual, by contact, and being built.
- [Terms](https://ranwhat.com/terms.md): the terms for Plus and the account: organisations, billing, cancelling, the 14-day refund, tokens.
- [About](https://ranwhat.com/about.md): who builds it and why
- [Updates](https://ranwhat.com/updates.md): every release, newest first, with an [RSS feed](https://ranwhat.com/rss.xml) and email signup
- [Source](https://github.com/MatijaMiki/ranwhat): MIT licensed
- [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/ranwhat/)
